issues.detail: The Greek 'του οντος' (of the Ontos) is translated as 'Giu-pi-tê'. While this may be a specific local name, it does not reflect the Greek text provided.

The Greek 'προ της πολεως αυτων' (before their city) is translated as 'có đền thờ trước thành' (having a temple before the city). The Greek does not mention a 'temple' (naos/hieros); it only specifies the location of the priests/offering.

The Greek 'στεμματα' (crowns/wreaths) is translated as 'vòng hoa' (flower garlands). While a common equivalent, 'vòng hoa' can sometimes imply a specific type of garland not present in the text, but more importantly, the translation of 'προ της πολεως' into a description of a temple building is a significant conceptual addition.
